A_target.statement:
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ be elements of a [[Definition:Commutative Ring|commutative ring]].
Then the [[Definition:Vandermonde Matrix|Vandermonde determinant]] satisfies:
:$\map \det {\mathbf V} = \det \begin {bmatrix} 1 & x_1 & \cdots & x_1^{n - 1} \\ \vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\ 1 & x_n & \cdots & x_n^{n - 1} \end {bmatrix} = \displaystyle \prod_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \paren {x_j - x_i}$

B_source.statement:
Let $P \in R \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ vanish whenever $x_i = x_j$.
Then:
:$\paren {x_j - x_i} \divides P$

substitutions.the polynomial P: det V as a polynomial in x_1,...,x_n
substitutions.the vanishing condition x_i = x_j: two equal rows making the determinant 0

object_map.reformulation: View the determinant as a polynomial; equal-argument vanishing forces each difference as a factor, and a degree count pins the constant.

validity_conditions: If x_i = x_j the matrix has two equal rows, so det V = 0; by the factor theorem (x_j - x_i) divides det V.
The product prod_{i<j}(x_j - x_i) therefore divides det V, and both have the same degree n(n-1)/2.
Comparing the leading coefficient (both 1) shows the quotient is 1, giving equality.
proof_plan: Regard $\map \det {\mathbf V}$ as a [[Definition:Polynomial over Ring|polynomial]] in $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ with integer coefficients.

If $x_i = x_j$ for $i \ne j$, rows $i$ and $j$ are equal, so $\map \det {\mathbf V} = 0$.
By the [[Factor Theorem]], each $x_j - x_i$ divides $\map \det {\mathbf V}$.

The factors are pairwise coprime, so their product divides $\map \det {\mathbf V}$.
Both have total degree $0 + 1 + \cdots + \paren {n - 1} = \dbinom n 2$.

The coefficient of $x_2 x_3^2 \cdots x_n^{n - 1}$ is $1$ on both sides, from the diagonal of $\mathbf V$ and from choosing $x_j$ in each factor.
Hence:
:$\map \det {\mathbf V} = \displaystyle \prod_{i \mathop < j} \paren {x_j - x_i}$
{{qed}}
